newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's GZI Transport seen poised for big debut.
newsitem.headline: HK's GZI Transport seen poised for big debut.

text.p: GZI Transport Ltd, the latest red chip to hit the Hong Kong market, is poised for a strong market debut this week, with its grey market price already indicating hefty gains for investors, analysts said on Tuesday.
Shares in the infrastructure spinoff of Guangzhou Investment Co Ltd are due to begin trading on Thursday.
Its public offering was 529 times subscribed and market sources said the stock was indicated at HK$5 to HK$6 per share in the grey market compared with an issue price of HK$3.23.
"I think the shares will trade around the grey market price due to the strong subscription and their red-chip concept," said DBS Securities director of research Percy Au-young.
Red-chip stocks are a favourite in the Hong Kong market, with investors anticipating that parent companies are likely to boost net asset values with asset injections.
Red chips are shares of Hong Kong-based companies either backed-up by Chinese parents or with strong mainland ties.

Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd, an investment arm of the Shanghai municipal government, has set a strong example. The stock, which was listed in May 1996, closed at HK$28.05 on Tuesday, compared with an issue price of HK$7.28.
GZI Transport initially issued 250 million new shares at HK$3.23 per share, with warrants on the basis of one warrant for every five shares.

Global coordinator Peregrine Capital Ltd exercised its overallotment option and 37.5 million additional shares were issued -- 22.5 million for international investors and 15 million for the Hong Kong public.

The additional issue brought the total for international placement to 172.5 million shares and for public offer to 115 million shares after 37.5 million shares were reallocated from the placement to the public offer.
Of the public offer, 83.75 million shares were available to the general public.
GZI Transport, through its parent, is indirectly linked to the Guangzhou municipal government.
"The company's roads are located mainly in some heavy traffic flow areas, and that helps in securing its future earnings," said Ben Kwong, research director at Dharmala Securities.
GZI Transport has invested in six toll road projects, including one under construction and one in pre-construction in China's southern province of Guangdong.

Analysts said expectations of future asset injections had made the stock an attractive buy, with Guangzhou Investment's links to Chinese authorities expected to help GZI Transport secure future toll road projects in China and acquire more assets.

GZI Transport, the first red-chip toll road concern to be listed in Hong Kong, has said it will use the proceeds of the initial public offering to finance investment in existing and future toll road projects in China.
